correctness.rationale: The exactly supported centered quadratic B-spline samples give a cosine sum with factor cos(pi nu). Three exhaustive lambda support chambers reduce its noncentral real-frequency zeros to a cubic, a quadratic, and an affine expression in y=cos^2(pi nu). Direct coefficient algebra and two exact negative Bernstein certificates prove the cubic has precisely one real root and that the quadratic has no positive root. The cubic root lies in (0,1) exactly before (99-2sqrt(42))/247. Polynomial derivatives settle both multiple-zero boundary cases. CHECK.py repeats exact identities and 40 supplementary assertions. No infinite conclusion is inferred from samples.
